topic: What orbital configurations justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication?
response: Orbital configurations with high satellite density and limited inter-satellite connectivity justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication. Specifically, for p ≤ 6, where p is the number of satellites in a plane, and with a communication range to ensure full inter plane connectivity of l(cid:2) adj(7, 40) = 3527 km, V-band offers better performance due to its higher bandwidth and lower latency compared to optical links.
reference_context: The reference context discusses the performance of satellite systems, including optical and RF links, in various orbital configurations. It highlights the importance of buffer size, data rate, and satellite density in determining system performance.
